You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input: matches = rlm.harness.search('horizontal stripes rows alternating sequence', kind='memory', limit=10, global_=True); [(m.title,m.content) for m in matches]
steps.output: [('ARC: periodicize full-width color stripes by stripe count', 'For ARC grids containing full-width horizontal solid-color stripes separated by background-zero rows: let N be the number of nonzero stripe rows. Treat row indices modulo N as the period. For each residue r, take the color of the input stripe at any row whose index mod N is r; fill every output row with the corresponding color across the full width. This preserves every original stripe and replaces all zero rows. Example task-82d6b2bb: stripes at rows 3=4, 5=7, 10=6 (0-based), N=3, so residues 0,2,1 map to 4,7,6 and output cycles [4,6,7] from row 0. Demos also confirmed the method with 9 stripes and 8 stripes: the period equals stripe count, and the sequence is determined by stripe row index modulo that count. Additional validation: a 10x10 input with six consecutive solid stripes at rows 2–7 colored [9,1,4,6,7,6] uses N=6, so rows 0–9 become [7,6,9,1,4,6,7,6,9,1] by row-index modulo 6.'), ('ARC alternating horizontal gaps fill with 2', 'For ARC grids with background 6 and repeated same-color markers in a row at every-other-column positions (e.g., color 1 in columns c, c+2, c+4, ...), fill each intervening background cell with color 2. Preserve the original markers and all other cells. Demonstration: in rows of color-8 markers spaced by one background cell, output inserts 2 between each adjacent pair; applies independently to multiple horizontal runs and rows. Do not fill gaps between markers on different rows.'), ('ARC task-82d6b2bb: complete sparse periodic color patterns', 'Task-82d6b2bb is to complete a periodic color pattern through zeros. Infer the shortest consistent period and its coordinate/orientation from colored cells; fill every cell, not just zeros, using the periodic mapping. For down-right diagonal bands, color depends on d=(c-r) mod p; each observed monochrome band gives the color for that residue. Solved example: p=5 with residues 0→1, 1→3, 2→5, 3→6, 4→9, so every output cell is [1,3,5,6,9][(c-r)%5]. Observations were 1 on d=-5, 3 on d=-4, 9 on d=-1, 6 on d=3, and 5 on d=7. Other verified example: a 14x14 input with down-right bands of colors 1,4,5,8 had p=4 and residue map (c-r)%4: 0→8, 1→5, 2→4, 3→1; output is a full diagonal periodic tile. If stripes are down-left use r+c instead. Horizontal full-row stripes are a special case of periodic completion; infer period and phase from observed row indices, then repeat. Prior demos: rows [0,4,2,9] became [9,4,2,9] (period 3); a stripe sequence with period 7 filled blank rows to match the repeating cycle. Do not assume zeros are background; use all clues to resolve period, axis and phase.'), ('ARC: fill gaps between alternating row marks with 2', 'For ARC grids containing horizontal runs of alternating marker/background cells, insert color 2 in each single background cell between horizontally adjacent marker cells, leaving endpoints and all other cells unchanged. Example: 0 7 0 7 0 7 becomes 0 7 2 7 2 7; for marker 8 on background 3, replace 3s in 8-3-8 patterns with 2. Process independently by row; do not extend beyond the outermost markers or alter background outside the gaps. Confirmed on task-29a3d32d.'), ('ARC diagonal stripes define periodic color tiling', 'For ARC grids containing sparse colored diagonal streaks on a zero background, infer the repeating tile from the streaks: count the distinct parallel diagonal color bands (often p colors), then fill the entire grid with a p-periodic pattern keyed by the diagonal coordinate. For streaks sloping down-right, use (c-r) mod p; for streaks sloping down-left (anti-diagonals), use (r+c) mod p. Each color band identifies the color assigned to its observed residue; extend that residue-to-color mapping across all cells, producing a fully tiled grid. Example: 15x15 clues had color 1 at r+c=5, color 2 at r+c=22, color 4 at r+c=27. p=3, mapping residue 2→1, 1→2, 0→4; output uses color by (r+c)%3. Another demo with four down-right diagonal bands yielded 4x4 cyclic tile mapping (c-r)%4: 0→9,1→5,2→8,3→3.'), ('ARC mirrored tripling of grid dimensions', 'Continual-ARC pattern: given an HxW input grid, output has size 3H x 2W. Each output row is formed by concatenating the row reversed left-to-right, then the original row. The output row sequence is reversed(input rows) + input rows + reversed(input rows). Demonstrations: 5x4 became 15x8; 1x7 became 3x14. For the 1-row case, reversing the one-row sequence gives three identical output rows. Be precise: vertical order is [rows reversed, rows forward, rows reversed], not simply triplicate each input row; source rows at each of the three positions in each output block follow this sequence.'), ('ARC: color the trailing gap after horizontal bars', 'Observed recurring ARC transformation: on rows containing a horizontal bar in a non-background color, fill the remaining background cells to the right edge with color 1, preserving the original bar and other cells. Demo: 11x19 rows had color-5 bars of lengths 16, 19, 13, 8; output filled their rightward gaps with 1s (row 19-wide bar unchanged). Solved test with color-6 bars: full-width row unchanged, 21-cell bar on a 26-wide row got five 1s at the right. Another demo showed trailing 1s in rows with rightmost color-7 bands. Apply only to rows exhibiting the bar pattern; leave other rows unchanged.'), ('ARC partial horizontal color-2 ray completion', 'Continual-ARC task pattern: On a uniform-background grid with multiple horizontal rows of a foreground color, a fully filled horizontal row can indicate the foreground color to use for incomplete horizontal runs elsewhere. Complete each partial horizontal run to the grid edge in color 1, leaving its original foreground segment intact and all other cells unchanged. Demos: full 4 row and partial 4 run toward right -> fill remaining right cells with 1; full 2 row and partial 2 runs starting at left or interior -> fill the remaining cells to the right edge with 1. In one noisy demo with patterned speckles, relevant partial row extensions also used 1. This solved task-07f79b91: row of 2s at row 3 full width, row 12 cols 0-10 in 2, fill cols 11-15 with 1.'), ('ARC task-4bf19258: copy occupied panel across horizontal divider', 'For recurring task-4bf19258, a grid is split into equal-sized panels by a solid horizontal divider. One panel is uniform background (example: all 9) and the other contains a pattern. Copy the occupied panel into the blank panel in the same relative coordinates; keep the divider and original occupied panel unchanged. Demonstration: 17x9 input had an 8x9 all-9 top panel, row 8 all 5, and an 8x9 pattern below. Output duplicated those bottom eight rows into the top eight rows, preserving row 8 and the original lower panel. This solved the test with zero wrong submissions.'), ('ARC task-07f79b91: color trailing background after horizontal 8 runs', 'For task-07f79b91, the grid has a uniform background (demo used 7; test used 0) and rows containing color 8. In each such row, find the rightmost 8 and recolor every background cell to its right through the grid edge as color 1. Preserve all cells up to/rightmost 8, including any gaps before that rightmost 8, and leave rows without 8 unchanged. A fully filled 8 row has no change. Demo validated this: on one fragmented 8 row, cells strictly right of its rightmost 8 became 1; the repeated row already filled with 8s stayed unchanged. Test solved by turning the 0 tail to 1 on two partial horizontal 8 rows.')]
